doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: First New York recordings: Richardson and Etta Jones date
summary: His first Prestige date led to more; the Etta Jones session was quick, with no rehearsal.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you recall the first recording date in New York that you made?

In New York. I think it was with Jerome Richardson. It was called “Roamin’ with Richardson” for Prestige. And that particular date I think the coordinator, somebody by the name of — oh I can’t think of his name — he got me on a lot of other dates for Prestige. That one date I did with Jerome did it, really. I got more calls from Prestige to do more dates. And as a result I did this date with Etta Jones, “Don’t Go to Strangers.” And that luckily, fortunately, turned out pretty good.
It’s curious when a record like that takes off. I’m wondering when you recorded it, did it make a particular impression on you?

No. Well usually I would go to a date and I would play it and then I didn’t think anymore about it because it seems like it would take them forever to release the record anyhow. By the time they released it I’d forgotten all about it really. I knew we did a good job on that, considering we, in those days you’d just go in the studio, there was no rehearsal, the A&R man as they were known in those days, would bring in some sheets of music and in © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
the case of a vocalist you may have to transpose the sheet and make up the arrangements on top of it, in six hours.
They could do an album in six hours.
Six hours or less. And that’s a lot of pressure. We did it though. Everybody did.
So you’d be at the piano and the singer would come over and let’s try this, and well can we do it—

Well the singer usually, well in the case of Etta Jones, she knew the tunes, she knew the keys, I think she did, and we would get it together and decide on the changes, quickly, very quickly. Figure out an intro, endings, and the solo, and that would be it. Some of those things we did were just one take. I think “Don’t Go to Strangers” was just one take.
